2. Heard Sri.Gaurav Subramanyam, learned counsel for the petitioner and Smt.K.P.Yashodha,
learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent -State. Perused the materials on record.
3.

In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the petitioner is entitled for grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.?"

My answer to the above point is in 'Negative' for the following:

sentences.text: The petitioner-accused No.1 is seeking grant of bail.
He was apprehended on 21.07.2023 and since then, he is in judicial custody.
It is stated that accused Nos.2 and 3 are already enlarged on bail, but the allegations made against the present petitioner is of serious nature.
The victim was hardly 15 years of age.
She was forcibly married by the petitioner and he committed penetrative sexual assault repeatedly.
After investigation, charge sheet is filed.
It is stated that the victim is already examined before the trial court and she has fully supported the case of the prosecution.
Under such circumstances, the contention of the petitioner that the act was with the consent of the victim cannot be accepted.
Looking to the nature and seriousness of the offence and also the fact that the trial has already begun, I am of the opinion that the petitioner is not entitled for grant of bail.

5. Accordingly, I answer the above point in the negative and proceed to pass the following:
NC: 2024:KHC:20914 ORDER
The petition is dismissed.
